title: Microsoft Teams: raise hand and speak on mic and camera in events with up to 100,000 attendees
summary: Hold: the briefing promises that an attendee's camera appears in the recording, but Microsoft excludes attendee video streams from recordings of large-audience events and has not documented an exception for this change. It also reports license-assignment automation as undocumented despite Microsoft's general Teams add-on licensing and Graph assignment documentation.

claims.claim: Current Learn documentation says raise hand is off and cannot be enabled for events with 20,001 to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: For events with 20,001 to 100,000 attendees, this feature is turned off in the scheduling form and can't be turned on by organizers.

claims.claim: Events optimised for large audiences use town hall policy settings.
claims.quote: When Optimize for large audience is on, the event uses town hall policy settings.

claims.claim: Attendees of events optimised for large audiences cannot turn on mic and camera on demand.
claims.quote: For example, attendees can't turn on their microphones and cameras on demand

claims.claim: The November 13, 2025 admin release notes describe organisers and presenters bringing raised-hand attendees on screen.
claims.quote: town halls organized by users with Teams Premium can allow attendees to raise their hand. Organizers and presenters can then bring attendees on screen to allow them to share their camera and microphone.
claims.fix: Qualify the historical sentence as 'Microsoft's admin release notes for November 13, 2025 describe a related capability for town halls organised by users with Teams Premium: attendees raise their hand, and organisers and presenters bring them on screen to share camera and microphone.'

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the planned expansion of raise hand above 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: '581720 Teams raise hand'; '100,000 raise hand default'; 'Teams events 100000 raise hand bring attendees on screen default external anonymous admin policy filter speech'. Opened feature comparison, plan-events, events-licensing and teams-admin; no expansion documentation found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the 100,000-attendee change uses the mechanism in the November 2025 notes.
claims.quote: Searched: '581720 Teams raise hand'; 'Teams events 100000 raise hand bring attendees on screen default external anonymous admin policy filter speech'. Opened teams-admin, plan-events and feature comparison; the roadmap does not identify the 2025 mechanism.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state of the planned change is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: '100,000 raise hand default'; 'Teams events 100000 raise hand bring attendees on screen default external anonymous admin policy filter speech'. Read roadmap, feature comparison, plan-events and teams-admin; current limits are stated, but no future default is stated.

claims.claim: No source states that the planned change modifies existing events automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: '100,000 raise hand default'; '581720 Teams raise hand'. Read roadmap, plan-events, feature comparison and teams-admin; no statement about automatic changes to already scheduled events found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: The planned feature lets an audience member speak on mic and camera during an event of up to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Ask your questions live and take part in the conversation, even at events with up to 100,000 attendees. Organizers can then let people with a raised hand turn on their mic and camera to ask their question or speak during the event.

claims.claim: Anyone watching the recording will hear and see the attendee brought on mic and camera.
claims.quote: Meeting recordings don't capture: ... Attendee video streams in events optimized for large audiences and in live events
claims.fix: Remove 'and by anyone who later watches the recording' from the Data exposure bullet. Microsoft excludes attendee video streams from large-audience event recordings at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-recording-policy; no source read states an exception for the planned on-screen capability.

claims.claim: Record events optimized for a large audience defaults to On.
claims.quote: | Record events optimized for a large audience | On | When On, organizers can record events optimized for large audiences. |

claims.claim: No documented filter checks what an attendee says or shows through the planned mic and camera capability.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams raise hand filter speech'; 'Teams town hall recording attendee brought on screen microphone camera recording filters speech'. Opened plan-events, settings-policies-reference and manage-meeting-presentation-experience; no attendee speech/camera content filter found.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Who can attend events optimized for a large audience defaults to Everyone, allowing any user to attend.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone. When users with this policy create events with up to 1,000 attendees or events optimized for large audiences, any user can attend.

claims.claim: The attendance policy restricts who may attend large events created by organisers assigned that policy.
claims.quote: Controls who can attend events optimized for large audiences (such as town halls) created by organizers with this policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether external or anonymous attendees can be brought on mic and camera in this planned expansion.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams events 100000 raise hand bring attendees on screen default external anonymous admin policy filter speech'. Read roadmap, feature comparison, plan-events and teams-admin; no eligibility statement for external or anonymous speakers in this expansion found.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI or API switch is documented to allow or block raise hand and bringing attendees on screen in large events.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams town hall raise hand bring on screen admin setting policy Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy'; 'town hall raise hand policy'. Read Events policies table, Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy syntax, plan-events and manage-reactions-meetings; no dedicated enforcing switch found.

claims.claim: The large-event creation control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents large-event creation.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled
claims.fix: Add 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the policy as preview' to the notes for controls[1] and controls[2]. The reference at https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy says 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.' Keep the roadmap's General Availability release phase unchanged.

claims.claim: Disabling large-event creation is a broad fallback rather than a raise-hand-only restriction.
claims.quote: Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.claim: Turning the creation setting Off after scheduling prevents the organiser running or starting the event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: The attendance control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests restricts large-event attendance to the organisation and guests.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.claim: An organiser's attendee pack can be changed at Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Attendee pack.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. On the Licenses tab, in the Attendee pack column of the table, select the drop-down in the user's row, and then choose the pack size that you want.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for assigning attendee pack add-on licenses to organisers.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. ... POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].api with kind 'graph', call 'POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/user-assignlicense?view=graph-rest-1.0'. Add the note 'General user-license assignment: addLicenses specifies the purchased license skuId; removeLicenses identifies licenses to remove.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-add-on-licensing/assign-teams-add-on-licenses, which documents PowerShell assignment of Teams add-on licenses. Narrow the prose to 'The Manage Attendee Capacity Pack page describes the Teams admin center workflow; general Teams add-on license assignment is also documented through Microsoft Graph.' Do not invent a pack-specific SKU identifier.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Scope: Admin roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: Managing attendee packs in the Teams admin center License Management section requires Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Scope: Admin roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams Administrator has read-only access to the License Management section.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each organiser can be assigned only one attendee pack.
claims.quote: While your organization can purchase multiple packs, each organizer can only be assigned one pack.

claims.claim: The Reactions default is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Reactions.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit. Under Meeting engagement, turn the Reactions toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMeetingReactions Disabled sets the Reactions default to Off.
claims.quote: To set the default value for meeting reactions to Off for organizers with the policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMeetingReactions Disabled

claims.claim: Reactions sets a Meeting options default that organisers may change for each meeting and event.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can use the Teams admin center or PowerShell to set the default value for reactions in your organizers' Meeting options. Organizers can change the setting for each meeting and event they create.

claims.claim: Learn says turning reactions off disables hand raise.
claims.quote: If you choose to turn off reactions, remember that this option disables the hand-raise feature.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed: base event features plus a capacity add-on for larger engaged events.
claims.quote: Organizers with a license in the Advanced event features category have all foundational event capabilities plus the following advanced event features. ... With an Attendee Capacity Pack, organizers can scale events up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Advanced event features, including raise hand, are listed for Office 365 E1, E3, E5 and Microsoft 365 E3, E5, E7.
claims.quote: | Enterprise | Not applicable | Office 365 E1, E3, E5Microsoft 365 E3, E5, E7 | ... Attendee reactions, raise hand, and polls

claims.claim: Advanced event licences support engagement features for up to 3,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Engaged events above 3,000 attendees require an Attendee Capacity Pack assigned to the organiser, subject to the stated legacy Teams Premium exception.

claims.claim: Teams Enterprise capacity and attendee pack capacity are not combined.

claims.claim: Attendee packs increase capacity without unlocking other feature capabilities.

claims.claim: An active Teams Premium licence purchased before April 1, 2026 retains hosting capacity up to 100,000 attendees until its current term ends.

claims.claim: Capacity is not updated automatically on events already scheduled when pack assignments change.
